newsitem.title: INDIA: Five tribal militants killed in northeast India.
newsitem.headline: Five tribal militants killed in northeast India.

text.p: Indian soldiers killed five tribal guerrillas on Wednesday near the border with Burma as insurgency-related violence mounted ahead of a national holiday commemorating 50 years of independence, police said.

A gunbattle erupted when soldiers went to raid a hideout belonging to separatist militants in Thoubal district in the northeastern state of Manipur, police in the state capital Imphal told Reuters by telephone.

All five guerrillas involved in the gunbattle were killed, and the soldiers recovered arms and ammunition, they said. Police said they had identified the insurgents but declined to disclose the name of their group.
More than a dozen tribal guerrilla groups in the remote mountainous state of Manipur have been fighting for independence for several decades.
On Tuesday, four separatist groups in Manipur urged people to boycott the nation's independence day celebrations by staying at home for 23 hours starting at 7 p.m. (1330 GMT) on Thursday.
India marks its 50th anniversary of independence from British colonial rule on August 15.
The hilly, heavily-forested region is surrounded by Burma, Bangladesh, Bhutan and China, and is linked to the rest of India by a 20-km (12-mile) wide corridor.
In neighbouring Assam state, Bodo tribal guerrillas on Wednesday attacked an army vehicle, injuring three soldiers, and blew up a bridge, police in the state's biggest city Guwahati said.
A Bodo militant group on Monday killed 12 Hindus, executing six after tying them to a tree, in a series of attacks on villages in Assam.
Bodo guerrillas have recently stepped up their campaign to have an independent homeland for their tribe's 600,000 members carved out of the oil- and tea-rich state.
Bodo guerrillas have their camps in the foothills of southern Bhutan and accuse Bengali-speaking Hindu immigrants of encroaching on their homeland in Assam.
